parts.text: A sample contains atoms of a particular isotope of protactinium .

parts.label: a
parts.text: A nucleus of this protactinium isotope contains 91 protons and 143 neutrons. (a) State the values of X and Y in the symbol . (i) X = ................................................................. Y = ................................................................. [2] This isotope is radioactive and it decays by the emission of a β -particle, β , to an isotope of uranium, U. Complete the equation for the decay of a protactinium nucleus. (ii) β + U ............. ............. Pa ............. ............. 0 –1 [2]

parts.label: b
parts.text: A radiation detector measures a background count rate in a laboratory of 32 counts/minute. (b) Suggest two naturally occurring sources of background radiation. (i) 1. ............................................................................................................................ 2. ............................................................................................................................ [2] The sample is placed in the laboratory close to the radiation detector, and the count rate increases to 544 counts/minute. This isotope of protactinium has a half-life of 400 minutes. Predict a value for the count rate measured 1200 minutes later. (ii) count rate = ....................................................... [4] Suggest one reason why the count rate measured 1200 minutes later may differ slightly from the value predicted in (b)(ii) . (iii) ................................................................................................................................ ................................................................................................................................ [1]

ms.label: 10(b)(i)
ms.text:
any two lines from:
rocks (buildings / earth / ground / wood / stone / minerals)
space (Sun / stars / galaxies / cosmic rays)
air (radon)

ms.text:
